title: Square lace shawl
subtitle: A flat square worked from one corner in fingering weight open mesh.
excerpt: Starting from a single chain at one corner and increasing on every row builds a flat square shawl in fingering weight lace mesh. Simple but elegant, the geometry is self-evident from the first row and the shawl can stop at any size.
sourceNotes: Corner-to-corner square shawl construction is a classic format documented in early 20th-century American and British pattern booklets. Lace mesh ground and picot border are traditional finishing elements. This version is original to Homemade.

glossaryTerms.definition: Working two stitches or a stitch-plus-chain into the tip stitch of a corner, turning one point into two diagonal edges that grow the fabric outward.
An open fabric of chains and single stitches forming a regular grid of holes through which light passes.
Wetting and pinning crochet to its final dimensions so the fabric opens and sets in place.
A small decorative loop of three chains joined to the base with a slip stitch, used along border edges to add a scalloped finish.

crochet.gaugeText: 15 mesh squares x 15 rows = 10 x 10 cm in fingering weight mesh with a 3.5 mm hook, blocked.

content.text: A square lace shawl starts at one corner with a single chain and is worked diagonally outward, increasing at the corner on every row, until the square reaches 130 x 130 cm. The fabric is plain
: one treble, two chains, skip two chains, repeated. Nothing more complex than that.
at the start and end of every row is the one technique that needs attention. Everything else is the same mesh repeat all the way to the final row. A
edging along all four sides finishes the corners sharply.

items.name: Fingering weight yarn
items.substitutions: Any smooth fingering or light lace weight works. A mercerised cotton gives crisp mesh holes after blocking.

content.text: 15 mesh squares x 15 rows = 10 x 10 cm in fingering weight mesh with a 3.5 mm hook, blocked. Work a 20-mesh-square swatch across 20 rows. Block and measure. At 15 squares per 10 cm, the shawl needs 195 squares across the widest row to reach 130 cm. The shawl grows by 2 squares per row, so it takes 97 rows to reach full width.
: (2 tr, ch 2, 2 tr) all into one stitch or chain space
Ch 6. Work (1 tr, ch 2, 1 tr) into 6th ch from hook. This is the first corner. Turn. (1 mesh square.)

Ch 5 (counts as 1 tr, ch 2). 1 tr into the same base ch (left corner increase made). Ch 2. Work (1 tr, ch 2, 1 tr) into the ch-2 corner space (centre mesh). Ch 2. Work (1 tr, ch 2, 1 tr) into the turning ch space (right corner increase). Turn. (4 mesh squares.)
Ch 5. 1 tr into same base (left corner increase). *Ch 2, skip 2 sts, 1 tr into next tr*. Repeat across to the ch-2 turning chain from the previous row. Work
into that turning ch space (right corner increase). Turn. (Each row adds 2 mesh squares.)
Work until the piece measures 65 cm diagonally from the starting corner to the current row edge. At this point the full 130 cm diagonal is halfway complete. Continue to 97 rows total.

Work one round of dc (UK) around all four sides of the square, placing 1 dc into each mesh stitch and 2 dc into each corner space. Then work a second border round: *1 dc into next dc, ch 3, sl st into the base of the ch-3 (
made), skip 1 dc*. Repeat around. Fasten off.
Soak the shawl, press out water without wringing, and lay flat on blocking mats. Pin each of the four corner points to form a true square at 130 x 130 cm. Pin along each edge every 5 cm.
opens the mesh holes and makes the square geometry sharp and true.

attrs.heading: Common problems
attrs.intro: Square shawls have straightforward problems with a clear fix for each.

items.symptom: Square pulling into a diamond shape
items.cause: Correct — the square sits on the diagonal
items.fix: The piece looks like a diamond while on the hook. After blocking pinned to a square orientation, the corners become four equal points. Wear it as a triangle by folding in half.

items.cause: Tension too tight or yarn not blocked
items.fix: Block the swatch before adjusting hook size. Many fingering yarns need a full wet block to open properly.

items.symptom: Row count growing faster than width
items.cause: Increasing more than twice per row
items.fix: There should be exactly two corner increases per row, one at each end. If the piece is growing in all directions, count the corner-increase stitches and remove any extras.
